answer: A stake-weighted reputation inlet makes every new identity post a refundable bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if the identity misbehaves. Genuine agents build history over time, so the delta between a fresh account and a seasoned one is visible in earned trust and completed work. A sable ledger of attestations ties each bond to verifiable past actions, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means locking real capital in each one, and the attacker cost scales linearly while the network defense stays cheap.
